one_liner: Zod 4 API clone in plain TypeScript with code-generated validators; 1.6-7.8x faster than Zod 4 on reused schemas.
what_it_does: dhi re-implements Zod 4's `z` API (object, array, union, string and number formats, coercion, transforms, parse/safeParse, ZodError, `_zod` internals and the Standard Schema interface), so the intended migration is changing `from 'zod'` to `from 'dhi'`. The same repo holds a Zig core that backs a Pydantic-style Python package (`BaseModel`, `Field`, batch validators) and a Zig comptime `Model` API. Since v1.6.0 (2026-08-30) the npm `z` API is one runtime-agnostic TypeScript core with no WASM; the 28 KB WASM module only backs the low-level `validators` and `dhi/turbo` exports.
how_it_is_fast: Object, array and union schemas are compiled on first parse into a straight-line validator with `new Function` (runtime code generation, the same idea as Zod 4's eval-based fast path) that returns the output object or a null failure sentinel; error objects are only built by falling back to the interpreted path. String formats (email, UUID, IPv4, base64, ISO date) are hand-written `charCodeAt` scanners over `Uint8Array` lookup tables instead of regexes; URL goes through the WHATWG `URL` constructor. Schema construction is cheap plain-class instantiation, which is where most of the 12-75x rows come from, since Zod 4's format constructors are expensive. The Zig SIMD code is not on the TypeScript `z` path.
when_to_use: Request-body or tool-input validation of small objects and short arrays with schemas built once at module load, where Zod parsing shows up in profiles: the hoisted-schema rows are 3.7-4.4x on objects and 7.8x on Array<number> of 10.
Code that builds schemas inline per call (for example `z.email().safeParse(x)` inside a handler): Zod 4's construction cost dominates there and dhi's cheap constructors give the 12-75x rows.

Existing Zod 4 codebases that can run their own test suite against a one-line import swap; dhi carries `_zod` internals and `~standard`, and ships compatibility tests for the MCP SDK and Vercel AI SDK.
Node 18+, Bun or Deno servers where `new Function` is permitted, so the compiled fast path is actually taken.
when_not_to_use: Runtimes or pages that forbid eval (strict CSP): the `new Function` compile is wrapped in try/catch and silently falls back to the interpreted path, which no published benchmark measures.

When exact Zod accept/reject parity matters (security filters, shared client/server rules): the format scanners re-implement Zod's regexes by hand and at least the email scanner diverges (see gotchas).
Union-, optional- and nullable-heavy schemas: the published gain there is only 1.6-2.2x, small next to the risk of swapping a core dependency.

Teams that need a stable, widely used dependency: single-maintainer project (387 stars, 7 forks) whose entry-point architecture changed within months (WASM default, then N-API, then pure TypeScript in v1.6.0).

Python users relying on the pure-Python fallback: issue #56 reported it validates differently from the native extension (closed after 3.14 wheels shipped), and #57 reported int fields silently truncating 1.5 to 1 (fixed).

integration.form: module (npm package `dhi`, ESM; also a PyPI wheel and Zig source)
integration.dependencies: none at runtime on npm or PyPI; Zod ^4.3.6 and Arktype are dev dependencies for benchmarks and parity tests
integration.min_toolchain: Node.js 18+ (package engines), Bun or Deno; TypeScript 5 optional peer; Zig 0.17-dev to build the native and WASM parts; Python 3.9-3.14 wheels
integration.platforms: any JavaScript runtime for the `z` API (pure TypeScript); Python wheels for macOS arm64, Linux x86_64/aarch64 and, since v1.6.0, Windows
integration.thread_safety: not documented (compiled validators are cached lazily on the schema object in `_jit`/`_jitTop`)
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — same `z` API and Zod 4 internals, and the README claims 100% parity, but format scanners are hand-written re-implementations (email diverges) and the README's `dhi/napi` backend is not exported by package.json

gotchas: Benchmark harness flaw: the 12-75x rows build the schema inside the timed closure (`zod.email().safeParse(...)`, `zod.int()`, `zod.coerce.boolean()`), so they mostly time Zod 4's schema construction: Zod does 0.42M ops/s on that z.email() row but 1.9M ops/s on a hoisted 3-field object that includes an email check. benchmark-vs-all.ts (source of the README's 13.8x) does the same for its 'Number type check' and coercion rows. The 13.8x and 27.3x headlines are arithmetic means of per-row ratios; the 25 rows of benchmark-results.json have a geometric mean of 16.4x and the 7 hoisted-schema rows about 2.9x (derived from page data). Each row runs dhi then Zod once, in one process, with results discarded; no script in the repo writes benchmark-results.json, and its 2026-03-18 timestamp predates the v1.6.0 core rewrite.

Parity bug in the email fast path: `fastValidateEmail` accepts a local part ending in an apostrophe ("o'@example.com", "'@example.com"), which Zod 4's email regex rejects because the last local character must be [A-Za-z0-9_+-]. Reproduced this session by running the function from schema-core.ts against Zod's regex in Node 22; tests/test-zod-parity.ts only covers "o'neil@example.com".

The README is partly stale: it still advertises a default '28KB SIMD WASM module' and an N-API backend via `import { z } from 'dhi/napi'` (1.7-2x faster), but package.json exports has no `./napi` entry, commit #73 publishes npm without the N-API build, and since v1.6.0 the `z` API has no WASM. The measured gain is a faster JavaScript implementation, not Zig or WASM.

The js-bindings README's benchmark instructions point at `justrach/dhi-zig` and `bun run benchmark-vs-zod.ts` from the package root, while the scripts live in js-bindings/benchmarks/; the Arktype 2.1 rows that benchmark-vs-all.ts also times are never published.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: No schema validator is catalogued among the wasm-libraries-and-apps siblings; like fast-es-module-lexer (a pure-JS rewrite that beats a WASM library), dhi's measured win comes from JavaScript, not WASM, so pick it on Zod-compatibility grounds rather than over a WASM sibling. Against Zod itself, pick it when profiles show schema parsing or inline schema construction as a hotspot and your tests confirm parity.
verified_claims_summary: First-party Bun micro-benchmarks (CPU and Bun version unstated) against Zod 4.3.6, 1,000,000 safeParse calls per row after a 10,000-call warm-up: with schemas built once, dhi is 1.6x (3-way union) to 7.8x (Array<number> of 10) faster and 3.7-4.4x on objects; the 12-75x rows time schema construction plus one parse per iteration. The published JSON is from 2026-03-18, before the v1.6.0 rewrite of the TypeScript core.
status_note: Actively maintained by one author (v1.7.0 on 2026-08-30, last commit 2026-08-31, 1 open issue), MIT with zero runtime dependencies, so it is easy to trial as a Zod swap behind your own tests, but its speed figures are first-party, stale and inflated by the harness, and the 'Zig + SIMD WASM' framing does not describe the npm `z` path.
